definition: Modeled habitat quality, or its mean over the indicated spatial support. National land and species-equal means weight different units.
Fifth percentile within each species range in the given year. Group summaries average species-specific P5 values. Global extraction uses fractional area weights.
Fraction of valid range habitat below the applicable low-quality cutoff, multiplied by 100. China uses HQ <= 0.239. Global uses HQ < 0.2814.
Global-flow sensitivity comparison using HQ <= 0.239.
Upper edge of the common-land background histogram bin containing the fifth percentile.
Unique 10-km analytical cell key in the published attribution, HQ, residual and trend tables.
Original model grid identifier, linked one-to-one to grid_id in grid_key.csv. Join using the explicit keys.
Projected cell coordinates from the annual runs. WGS 84 Albers, central meridian 105 E, standard parallels 25 N and 47 N, latitude of origin 0. See grid_coordinates.prj.
Training or held-out test membership of each grid for the named year (Train/Test).
IUCN species identifier. Use with year and, globally, scope to join analytical tables.
Taxonomic group. Case and display names can differ between source tables.
LC, NT, VU, EN or CR. Threatened comprises VU, EN and CR.
Number of annual valid exposure records and inclusion in the complete 21-year analytical cohort.
Province abbreviation in figure tables. 266 mapped grids have no assigned province. EN in category fields means Endangered.
Annual observations cover 2000 through 2020 inclusive.
Annual maximum Normalized Difference Vegetation Index.
Gridded total gross domestic product at purchasing power parity in 2017 international dollars.
Annual precipitation and annual mean temperature derived from monthly records.
Annual mean population count per valid 30-arc-second LandScan cell inside each 10-km analysis grid. Fig. 7 displays 2020 people per original cell above 200.
Gridded fossil-fuel carbon dioxide emissions (ODIAC).
Annual terrestrial Human Footprint Index used for attribution.
Elevation and terrain slope. Static model-input fields, with year-specific attributions.
Growing season length, warm spell duration index and cold spell duration index.
Local signed SHAP contributions; year suffix identifies the annual model. Model-input columns with similar names hold predictor values.
Arithmetic mean of signed contributions or of their absolute magnitudes across the 96,649 grids.
Mean absolute contribution of one driver divided by the sum of the 12 driver means for the same year, times 100.
Magnitude of negative or positive contributions of HFI, POP, GDP and CE, respectively, divided by the sum of absolute SHAP across all 12 drivers plus 1e-6, times 100.
Value in 2020 minus value in 2000. Relative change divides the difference by the 2000 value and multiplies by 100.
InVEST HQ, model prediction and their difference (Observed minus Predicted). Residuals refer to the annual prediction run.
Annual OLS slope for a cell, its standard error and pointwise 95% t interval (19 residual degrees of freedom).
Two-sided unadjusted OLS slope test. The archive records blank p values for 1,292 constant series.
Mean of a species' annual values over the study period, subsequently summarized across eligible species.
Sample size for the specified grouping; SEM is the sample SD divided by the square root of n.
Tie-corrected Kruskal–Wallis statistic, degrees of freedom and unadjusted p value.
Rank eta squared for the Kruskal–Wallis H test: max(0,(H-k+1)/(n-k)), where k is the number of groups. Historical field epsilon_squared has the same stored values.
Welch t and group 1 minus group 2 mean difference, or Mann–Whitney U for group 1 and rank-biserial effect 2U/(n1*n2)-1.
Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment among pairwise comparisons within the same metric and grouping variable.
Pointwise 95% effect limits: Welch t interval or stratified species percentile bootstrap for rank effects.
Mann–Kendall trend statistic expressed as tau and two-sided tie- and continuity-corrected p value.
OLS or Sen slope across the 21 annual aggregate values. Low-quality area changes are in percentage points.
Spatial autocorrelation of train and test residuals. The OLS/RF model-comparison reference reports the larger permutation p of the two sets.
Built-up (urb), cropland (crp), transport (rr). Archived distances in metres are converted to km for InVEST 3.14.2.
Road and railway infrastructure rasterized at 300 m; ordinary roads use the 1993 baseline for 2000–2012, with annual updates for 2013–2020.
GRIP4 road network held fixed throughout 2000–2020.
Land-cover class, suitability, and class-specific sensitivities to built-up land, cropland and transport; interpret columns by file.
Global includes China; other scopes are China and individual realms. The species group is all eligible or threatened species.
Common-valid within-range area including fractional cell overlaps, and number of intersecting cells.
OLS slope of the 21 annual species-range means or fifth percentiles, on fixed spatial support.
OLS rate of change in the within-range share below the global cutoff.
Equal-species estimate and 95% whole-species bootstrap limits for the named effect or trajectory.
Each year's estimate minus its 2000 value and paired-trajectory bootstrap limits.
Display-grid support in underlying valid 1-km cells, 2000 HQ, annual HQ trend and Mollweide bounds. Reprojected with nearest-neighbour sampling for Fig. 4.
Auxiliary within-range Human Footprint endpoint means on common support and their 2020 minus 2000 difference.
